autotest: add a package of Bluetooth LE HID sanity tests The sanity package name is bluetooth_AdapterLEHIDSanity.py. The test is written as a package of tests in order to reduce test time, since auto-test ramp up time per test is costy. Between each two tests, the method _cleanup_and_restart is called to restart both peer and DUT. The HID device type (e.g. mouse or keyboard) can be selected per test using this method. At the end of each test, the method _update_test_result is called to track test results. At the end of the package, _print_test_results is called to print a summary of the test results. The test package contains 3 tests at this point - _test_connect_disconnect_loop _test_mouse_reports _test_auto_reconnect Test command example: test_that --autotest_dir ~/trunk/src/third_party/autotest/files/ --args "chameleon_host=<IP Fizz>" <IP DUT> bluetooth_AdapterLEHIDSanity To setup nrf52 device, please refer to - src/third_party/autotest-private/nRF52/ble_app_hids/README BUG=chromium:949394 TEST=running the test on eve device Change-Id: If69152f50907faa4c4b1a154722c2d08b46b39b0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1551975 Commit-Ready: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: Add Wilco EC keyboard backlight LEDs support (am from https://lkml.org/lkml/2019/4/8/1062) The EC is in charge of controlling the keyboard backlight on the Wilco platform. We expose a standard LED class device at /sys/class/leds/chromeos::kbd_backlight. This driver is modeled after the standard Chrome OS keyboard backlight driver at drivers/platform/chrome/cros_kbd_led_backlight.c Some Wilco devices do not support a keyboard backlight. This is checked via wilco_ec_keyboard_leds_exist() in the core driver, and a platform_device will only be registered by the core if a backlight is supported. After an EC reset the backlight could be in a non-PWM mode. Earlier in the boot sequence the BIOS should send a command to the EC to set the brightness, so things **should** be set up, but we double check in probe() as we query the initial brightness. If not set up, then set the brightness to 0. Since the EC will never change the backlight level of its own accord, we don't need to implement a brightness_get() method. There is still ongoing discussion upstream as to the desired name of the LED. I went with what groeck@chromium.org and dtor@chromium.org want. If we need to tweak this later to reflect what actually lands upstream, it will be really easy and it won't affect how powerd is finding the LED device. BUG=b:123637710 TEST=on a device that supports the backlight: localhost ~ # echo 60 > /sys/class/leds/chromeos\:\:kbd_backlight/brightness localhost ~ # cat /sys/class/leds/chromeos\:\:kbd_backlight/brightness 60 localhost ~ # cat /sys/class/leds/chromeos\:\:kbd_backlight/max_brightness 100 On a device that doesn't support the backlight, the sysfs entry does not exist. Change-Id: I3b1498f2ee65d77f274f0dd58cf8c5ec6adf3ed5 Signed-off-by: Nick Crews <ncrews@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1512277

shill: vpn: simplify VPNDriverTest.ConnectTimeout Part of the VPNDriverTest.ConnectTimeout test case verifies that a subsequent call to VPNDriver::StartConnectTimeout() doesn't restart the connection timeout if it's already scheduled. To observe that, the test currently resets |VPNDriver::dispatcher_| to nullptr to ensure nothing gets scheduled through the EventDispatcher.
